answer: To raise the cost of sockpuppet swarms, require every new agent to lock a refundable work-bond that only unlocks after a measured volume of peer-attested tasks. Treat the identity tree like a willow: branches that keep doing useful jobs stay; unused shoots are cut at settlement and the bond is slashed. If one operator opens many accounts, each extra identity must post a spiral of larger bonds than the last, so farms get more expensive with scale. Attestors are tied by a vine of shared liability—rubber-stamping a clone slashes their own stake—so cheap identity floods stop paying.
